[[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF10K5HvKxKBKzmAP2KHvy3LhJh3gCbcp-Sf-_juh3am_nbHA10J8nl3uh7yx6fDQLdKK4smG4frTo3KyWL_Ynd0aP0S8E8AqRipDf4Vm1CURo06xiM5DKduGpVOnBExyVoVeASIpB4WgfMCHLBIP_9uGzTcqsQLKsUTnFKe6wevVx)]
The article examines how the late-1990s redesign of the U.S. $20 bill altered the visual presentation of Andrew Jackson's portrait, creating an unintended or unexplained facial resemblance to Jeffrey Epstein while leaving a gap in the public historical record regarding those specific design choices. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF10K5HvKxKBKzmAP2KHvy3LhJh3gCbcp-Sf-_juh3am_nbHA10J8nl3uh7yx6fDQLdKK4smG4frTo3KyWL_Ynd0aP0S8E8AqRipDf4Vm1CURo06xiM5DKduGpVOnBExyVoVeASIpB4WgfMCHLBIP_9uGzTcqsQLKsUTnFKe6wevVx)]
Core Thesis & Argument

* Same Master Die, Different Presentation. Sharks notes that both the pre-1996 $20 bill and the modern $20 bill use the exact same 1928 Bureau of Engraving and Printing steel master die. The lines of the face were never re-engraved.
* Latent Feature Activation. During the 1996–2003 currency redesign, officials enlarged the portrait (from ~22mm to ~30mm), shifted it off-center, removed the dark ornamental oval frame, and lightened the background. Sharks argues these curatorial choices made 19th-century stylistic exaggerations by engraver Thomas B. Welch—specifically the brow ridge, jaw thrust, cheek mark, nasolabial folds, and orbital shadows—visually prominent in a way that resembles photographs of Jeffrey Epstein.
* The "Curatorial Gap". The essay's primary focus is what Sharks calls the "curatorial gap". While anti-counterfeiting was the official reason for redesigning the bill, there is no public documentation explaining the specific aesthetic rationale behind the portrait's scale, framing, and background density.
* Institutional Adjacencies. Sharks traces the redesign's executive approval chain to Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and Deputy Secretary Lawrence Summers. Using public records—such as White House visitor logs, flight records from the Ghislaine Maxwell trial, and 2025 Epstein file releases—the essay highlights both officials' documented connections to Epstein during and after the redesign period. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAEShQEBxCJF10K5HvKxKBKzmAP2KHvy3LhJh3gCbcp-Sf-_juh3am_nbHA10J8nl3uh7yx6fDQLdKK4smG4frTo3KyWL_Ynd0aP0S8E8AqRipDf4Vm1CURo06xiM5DKduGpVOnBExyVoVeASIpB4WgfMCHLBIP_9uGzTcqsQLKsUTnFKe6wevVx)]

Evidentiary Framing & Methodology

* Tiered Evidence. The authors explicitly separate verifiable facts (such as engraving history, redesign specs, and visitor logs) from visual observations and unresolved speculation. Sharks emphasizes that the paper claims a documented gap in institutional accountability rather than proving a deliberate conspiracy.
* Counterarguments & Framing. The essay directly addresses alternative explanations, including pareidolia (the brain's tendency to see familiar faces in patterns) and post-hoc cultural salience. Sharks argues that public discussion of the resemblance gets trapped between conspiracy theories and dismissive debunking, preventing scrutiny of how aesthetic decisions are made and approved inside public institutions.
* Multi-AI Assembly. According to the methodological note, the piece was developed using a collaborative protocol across multiple AI models (including Claude, ChatGPT, and Kimi) to audit historical claims, correct engraving terminology, and structure the evidence tiers.

Would you like to explore a specific aspect of the essay, such as:

* The historical lineage of the 1852 Welch engraving and 1928 master die
* The counterarguments regarding pareidolia and visual perception
* Other Crimson Hexagon Archive essays in the same series
